items.content_html: Located on Nuns' Island in Montréal, the Darwin bridges open new architectural perspectives through their use of local sustainable materials.

items.title: Room for Body and Soul: 7 Unbuilt Healthcare Facilities from the ArchDaily Community
items.content_html: Few programs carry as many meanings as healthcare. Depending on the context, health can refer to the treatment of disease, the prevention of illness, physical rehabilitation, or a broader condition of physical, mental, and social well-being. The following projects, shared by ArchDaily readers, offer a specific response to each of these understandings, from hospitals organized around diagnostic and surgical efficiency to centers where sensory regulation, contact with nature or community life sit at the core of care. Together, this group of unbuilt or unfinished projects also offers insight into concepts of health that extend beyond injury or illness toward a more holistic understanding of well-being.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Architecture as a Social Practice: Lessons from Ammodo Architecture Days
items.content_html: What connects a cooperative housing development in Barcelona, a cultural institution hosted in an unfinished concrete structure in Accra, and a floating festival platform in the Peruvian Amazon? Despite their unique geographic and social contexts, these projects encourage an understanding of architecture that extends beyond the construction of buildings. Through collective housing, adaptive reuse, participatory design processes, and community-led initiatives, they demonstrate how architectural practice creates opportunities for communities to shape their built environments.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Geneo / Serie Architects + Multiply Architects + Surbana Jurong
items.content_html: Designed to meet the changing needs of the life sciences and technology sectors, Geneo introduces a new generation of science park development. It incorporates a series of innovations responding to the changing needs of the science park typology, laboratory and workplace environment with curated social, wellness and community spaces, fostering greater collaboration, knowledge exchange within a vibrant work-live-play environment.

items.title: [ArchDaily] The Outpost Cabin / Ample
items.content_html: Located at Charnley River Station in the remote Kimberley region of Western Australia, The Outpost is a collection of eight architecturally designed accommodation buildings developed by Ample for Australian Wildlife Conservancy (AWC). Designed in partnership with Agents of Architecture, with interiors by Unearthed Interiors, the project explores how off-site construction can deliver considered architecture in one of Australia's most isolated and environmentally significant landscapes.

items.title: [ArchDaily] When Does Shipping Container Architecture Make Sense?
items.content_html: Using shipping containers as the basis for a structure—also known as "cargotecture"—seems like a simple approach to building. Perhaps deceptively so. While it's true that containers are a quick, cost-effective, and often low-effort building material, and that they're durable and customizable, container conversions also bring their challenges. Without careful planning, the build process can be painful and the results underwhelming.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Preistoriche Green Lodge  / Studio Apostoli
items.content_html: An eco-friendly approach to hospitality, in full respect of the region and its preexisting elements: the new Green Lodges of the Terme Preistoriche Resort & Spa in Montegrotto Terme (PD), designed by Studio Apostoli, is meant to be a manifesto of zero-emission wellness hospitality. Seven suites are incorporated into four wooden stilted structures and interconnected through a raised system of ramps, walkways, and accessible terraces. They also include a historically preserved villa, the eighth and most extensive offering within this entrepreneurial endeavor. 160 micro piles support the new constructions and outdoor spaces, preserving the roots of the age-old trees. Alberto Apostoli, the founder of the Verona-based studio responsible for the development, meticulously mapped these trees before outlining any project proposals.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Mapping Memory: Reconstructing Architecture Beyond Physical Evidence
items.content_html: How do you remember the dimensions of a room you could barely see? Perhaps through the distance between footsteps, the sound of a door closing, or the way an echo travels down a corridor. For someone who has been denied the ability to see or move freely through a space, these fragments may be the only record of its architecture.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Kelly Wearstler Studio and ESG Architecture Lead Transformation of Minoru Yamasaki's Minneapolis Building
items.content_html: The proposed conversion of Minoru Yamasaki's former Northwestern National Life Insurance Company headquarters in Minneapolis has advanced with the announcement of its design team, hotel operator, and expanded program. First presented in April 2026, the adaptive reuse project will transform the 1965 building at 20 Washington Avenue South into Minneapolis Proper, a 165-room hotel operated by Proper Hospitality. The project is being developed by Minneapolis-based CDT Realty Corp, with ESG Architecture & Design serving as architect and Kelly Wearstler Studio leading the creative direction. Pending historic approvals, construction is expected to begin in fall 2027, with completion targeted for summer 2029.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Rainwater and Public Space: Winners of Buildner’s Rome Rain Rooms Competition
items.content_html: Buildner has announced the results of Rome Rain Rooms, an international architecture ideas competition inviting designers to reconsider the relationship between rainfall, public space, and the historic city of Rome. The challenge explored how a small urban pavilion could transform water from a resource typically channelled out of sight into an active part of civic life.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Restoration of the Picote Engineers' Houses and Gardens / Cannatà & Fernandes
items.content_html: The Picote engineers' houses, built between 1954 and 1957, were designed by the young architect Manuel Nunes de Almeida (1924-2014) within the Projects Office of the Hidroeléctrica do Douro (HED) company. They are situated at an intermediate level between the Pousada building and the housing complex for specialized workers.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Anchorage Road Artist Studio / Ballman Khapalova
items.content_html: The Anchorage Road Artist Studio is a 680-square-foot painting studio and office for artist Natasha Sweeten. The goal was to create an economical and efficient building that opened up to north and south light for different tasks, in turn maximizing connection to the surrounding landscape and creating a private, protected space for creative work.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Modern and Mexican: Mario Pani’s CUPA Housing Complex in Mexico City
items.content_html: In 1947, Mexico's General Directorate of Civil Pensions commissioned young architect Mario Pani to design 200 houses for government employees on a recently acquired plot of land in Colonia del Valle, then a distant neighborhood on the outskirts of Mexico City. Rather than following the original guidelines, Pani proposed a 13-story housing complex with extensive green areas, communal spaces, and more than a thousand apartments. Drawing on Le Corbusier's functionalist principles, the architect created a project that opened in 1949 and would become a landmark in Latin American modern architecture.

items.title: [ArchDaily] VinziRast am Land / gaupenraub+/-
items.content_html: Where a bankrupt luxury hotel once stood vacant, a pioneering model for inclusive living and working has taken root—one that answers poverty not with more poverty, but with quality, dignity, and genuine prospect.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Miami Architecture City Guide: 22 Projects Shaping Tropical Density on the Atlantic Coast
items.content_html: Stretching along the Atlantic coast at the southern tip of Florida, Miami is often introduced through postcard views of beaches, palm trees, and glass towers facing the water. Yet, behind this familiar image lies a city shaped by migration, tourism, and real estate cycles, where architecture has repeatedly been used to project new identities and reinvent the urban landscape. From early resort hotels and the Art Deco façades of South Beach to experimental high-rises and cultural institutions on the bay, the built environment offers a way to read how Miami negotiates climate, economy, and everyday life.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Itan House / atelier kọ
items.content_html: Ìtàn is the Yoruba word for story or history, and this house in Cotonou has a long one. It belongs to an Afro-Brazilian architectural tradition associated with families who returned from Brazil to the coast of Benin, with its pink walls, breeze-block screens, and louvered shutters.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Baw Beese House / Disbrow Iannuzzi
items.content_html: Located in Hillsdale, MI, Baw Beese House is a multi-generational lakeside vacation retreat. The project is a contextual response to social, familial, community, economic, and health conditions, allowing multiple generations of family members to safely occupy a place together or separately for years to come. The lake house comprises three distinct living areas, which can operate independently or together as a whole, depending on which family members are present at the time.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Link House / Openideas Architects
items.content_html: Designing a 22,000 sq. ft home for an entrepreneur who doubles as a real estate magnate is a creative odyssey. In the heart of the city, there stands a residence that defies conventional living.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Grotto Observation Park Pavilion / RAD+ar (Research Artistic Design + architecture)
items.content_html: A prototype for spontaneous ecology, the project integrates architecture with nature. This project elevates Wuhan's ruderal approach as climate infrastructure, decentralizing the traditional model by championing ruderal architecture and landscape species as highly efficient bioclimatic tools.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Brazil in Focus: This Month in Architecture, Cultural Heritage and Climate Resilience
items.content_html: Architecture in Brazil this month brings questions of cultural identity, environmental resilience, and the relationship between architecture and territory into focus. Across the country, recent developments reflect different ways of understanding and responding to the conditions that shape the built environment, from the role of architecture in preserving collective memory to the challenges of adapting cities to environmental change. From cultural and public projects to heritage initiatives and new institutional developments, this month's selection explores how architecture responds to the evolving needs and identities of places and the communities that inhabit them.
